name: WP Supra – Maintenance & Support Utilities
author: PR24

sections.description:
WP Supra is a modern WordPress management and maintenance tool designed for agencies, freelancers and advanced site owners.

The plugin serves two purposes:

  1. Connector to the WP Supra Management Panel for centralized multi-site administration
  2. Standalone maintenance toolkit with powerful utilities and optimizations

With WP Supra, you can manage multiple WordPress installations efficiently and maintain individual sites with advanced control.

WP Supra Management Platform

  • Centralized inventory of connected websites
  • Manage updates across multiple sites
  • Monitoring integrations
  • Cron job integrations
  • Free for up to 20 websites
  • Aforable price per additional site/month

Get Started

Take your WordPress maintenance to the next level with WP Supra.

🔍 Book an Audit or Consultation
Get expert insights into your WordPress setup and identify optimization potential:
https://wpsupra.com/get-started/

🧑‍💻 Create a WP Supra Account
Start managing multiple websites centrally:
https://wpsupra.com/sign-up/

Standalone Maintenance Features

🗒 Admin Notes
– Store important maintenance notes and instructions
– Example: “Do not install this plugin”
– Improve team collaboration and documentation

✅ Best Practices
– Built-in maintenance guidelines and recommendations
– Helps identify common configuration issues
– Encourages a consistent and professional maintenance workflow

✏️ Text Overrides
– Modify or replace text strings globally
– Not limited to translations
– No coding required

🔌 Integrations
– Matomo (self-hosted analytics, set up by WP Supra)
– Pulsetic (uptime monitoring, set up by WP Supra)
– Cloudflare (traffic and threat analytics, connected in WP Supra)
– Emailit (email delivery, read by WP Supra)
– All connected services on one statistics page (Dashboard → Analytics & Reports)

🔄 Update Management
– Control automatic updates
– Disable WordPress core updates
– Disable individual plugin/theme updates
– Clear overview of update status

📧 Email Enhancements
– Change admin email without 2FA confirmation
– Forward selected support emails
– Disable password change notifications
– Pause outgoing emails

⚡ Cache & Performance Overview
– Quick cache insights for troubleshooting
– Identify unused performance optimization potential
– Detect areas where caching can be improved

🖼 Media Management
– Overview of registered thumbnail sizes
– Manage media trash

🗄 Database Tools
– Manage revisions
– Clean up transients
– Table overview with storage usage and entry counts
– Identify unused tables and optimization potential

🔍 Advanced Database Analysis
– Meta data analysis with index suggestions
– Autoload optimization recommendations
– Slow query detection

🚧 Maintenance & Staging
– Maintenance mode
– Staging actions
– Website mode Live, Dev or Staging, shared with WP Supra

📊 System Status
– Maintenance-focused site health insights
– Simplified overview of critical system information
– Highlights relevant issues affecting maintenance and stability

🐞 Logging & Debugging
– Enable or disable WordPress debug mode
– Prevent excessive log file growth

If you are looking for regular WordPress maintenance, contact the team at WP Supra, WP Support or WP Support Schweiz. If you are looking for individual support, please contact the team at Support for WordPress and WooCommerce.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/support-wp directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Use the Settings > WP Supra screen to configure the plugin
sections.faq:
Is the Matomo API used?

Not by the plugin itself: WP Supra sets up the Matomo instance and delivers the core metrics shown in the dashboard. The plugin only prints the tracking code.

Is the Pulsetic API used?

Not by the plugin itself: WP Supra sets up the Pulsetic monitor and delivers the monitoring data shown in the dashboard.

Is the Cloudflare API used?

Not by the plugin itself: the Cloudflare API token is stored in WP Supra, which delivers the traffic figures shown in the dashboard. The plugin only knows the zone.

Does the plugin send data to external sources?

Only when the website is connected to WP Supra: the plugin then reads the monitoring and analytics figures from WP Supra and no longer calls the APIs of Matomo, Pulsetic, Cloudflare or Emailit itself. If Matomo is connected, the tracking code loads from the Matomo instance in the visitors’ browser. No data is transmitted without configuration by the administrator.

    • WordPress auto-updates pause while WP Supra updates the site; a rescue plugin keeps the update routes working

    • Extended compact notes to additional areas and improved note display

    • Added option to disable author pages

    • Added tweak relevant search

    • Added support for a comma-separated list of allowed IP addresses in Maintenance mode
    • Added a “Plugins with unknown update status” overview flagging plugins that use their own update mechanism instead of WordPress.org
    • Added detection of WordPress.com and Pressable hosting

    • Added option to disable all plugin updates or all theme updates at once
    • Added option to reinstall a plugin: re-downloads the currently installed version from WordPress.org and overwrites its files (e.g. to fix missing or corrupted files)
    • Reorganized the Cache overview into PHP-, shared-, WordPress-, HTTP- and plugin-level sections, with options to flush the object cache and reset OPcache
    • Reorganized the settings menu: Maintenance Mode, Rewrite Rules Repair and Staging Detection moved from Tweaks into their own dedicated sections; added explanatory info texts to several settings tabs

    • Fixed two potential SQL injection vulnerabilities.
    • Added developer notes regarding a low-risk IP spoofing scenario
    • Introduced the Major Plugins feature
    • Added new hints in the “Notes & Hints” section for major plugins, disabled plugin updates, and disabled theme updates.
    • Added new api endpoints
  • Version 104
    • Monitoring system rewritten to centralize all connections through the WordPress plugin, preventing multiple instances and improving stability.
  • Version 103
    • update endpoints and remove unused code
  • Version 102
    • More robust connection handling for the WP Supra Panel, improving overall stability and reliability.
    • Enhanced error handling and automatic reconnection mechanisms to better recover from temporary connection issues.
  • Version 101
    • Added a notice when WP Defender Audit Log is disabled.
  • Version 100
    • Fixed incorrect WooCommerce memory limit recommendations being displayed
    • Added support for Multisite notes and hint suppression
  • Version 99
    • Fixed WPMU DEV Hub SSO status detection for installations storing the setting as a boolean instead of an integer.
    • Added a notice when WP Defender Login Protection is disabled.

    • Corrections and Enhancements
